nodes.speaker: vesper
nodes.text: Smoke on the chimneys. Follow my draught, Kaelen, and they lose us in it.

nodes.speaker: kaelen
nodes.text: Stay low. Guard each other.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: The lock is iron and the seal is warm. Hold the bridge while I work it.

nodes.speaker: hollis
nodes.text: Get me a clear line down the canal rail.

nodes.speaker: kaelen
nodes.text: No more tolls. Force the Third Ward gate.

nodes.speaker: vesper
nodes.text: So much for quiet.

nodes.speaker: kaelen
nodes.text: Order 44 and a candle-gold shield, Vane. Your Seventh Ward sold its own.

nodes.speaker: captain_vane
nodes.text: Seal the grates behind me. The Watch remembers every face.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Those cage seals are cipher work. Keep the flagellants off the locks!

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: That silver saw. He used it on my mentor. Cut him down before the surge settles.

nodes.speaker: dunstan
nodes.text: My father's bones went down that chute. I will smash it before I die.

nodes.speaker: vesper
nodes.text: The tallow tithe killed my brother, an ash-sweeper. Count the fat that bought it, Orlov.

nodes.speaker: elyse
nodes.text: Hold the catwalk. I know these vats' pressure better than he does.

nodes.speaker: guild_master_orlov
nodes.text: Remember my name when the tallow runs short.

nodes.speaker: kaelen
nodes.text: The drain-vault has ruptured. Every valve we shut drove the marrow back down here, and now it is climbing the floor.

nodes.speaker: inquisitor_prelate_nemeth
nodes.text: Cold steel cannot finish me. Kneel at the winch.

nodes.speaker: kaelen
nodes.text: Someone hold that winch! The rest of you, run and do not look back.
Chirurgeon Sabina does not look up from the silver scalpel she is wiping on a strip of grey linen. "Mind the floor. It is wet, and not always with water."

choices.text: What do you do down here?
What did you ask me not to touch?
What do you make of the Prelate's valve?

nodes.text: "I cut what Cinderreach cuts into the young, and sometimes I put it back. The Slab does not open all at once. Bring me what the dead leave, and a cell that can stand to know what it is carrying, and I will see."

"The communion draught. Bone-sediment, ground fine, stirred into watered wine. I was an outer-ward prosector at twenty-one. I found the sediment in the commoners' draughts and said so, and Chief Anatomist Lazar sent Proctor Quell to teach me manners. The Spent are not old. They are fed."
"Quell's own retorts. I know that glass. A man who kept Maren's mentor alive on a table long enough to learn what he could take. The Slab can use them. I would rather it did not have to."

"Brass, hot to the touch, hungry. The Inquisition skims aberrant marrow, rots on it, and calls the rot purity. The Clerisy drinks the pure part. Keep that where I can look at it, and not near the Founders until I say."
Berek Dorn turns the loupe on his right eye toward you and lets a rivet drop into a tin. "Coals are hot. Don't breathe in. My lungs can take what yours can't."

choices.text: What did you cast for the Kiln?
Grendel's Slag-Hammer. Can you read it?

nodes.text: "Honest steel. Billhooks, heaters, the odd bodkin. Nothing fancy, nothing that dreams. When there's coin and a spare hour I'll put an edge back on whatever you bring. Not yet, though. I do the hard work in daylight, and there isn't any."

"Fifteen years, valves. Brass throats for what I swore were steam vents. Then Foundry-Master Jessop handed my apprentice Lucan to the Tithing to cover a cracked batch, and I traced the plans. They were made to pump a child's marrow up into the Cloisters. I won't say more until I've found where the pipe goes."
"Pneumatic piston-maul. Grendel's weight in black iron, and a lighter touch than it has any right to. I know the casting. I know the man. I would love to wear it, and I would love not to."
Talia Rusk does not turn her head to look at you. She turns the left ear, the one that still hears. "The board is on the wall. Chalk is ink down here. Read it twice."
"Bone rods, notches by the quarter-hour. Each rod is a runner. Each notch is a drop. If the Watch burns a rod, they've burned the runner, so keep the rods clean."

"Twelve. The fastest courier I ever taught after Vesper. The Watch has him in the Seventh Ward Toll-Pen with a number chalked on his shirt. If the Tithing hits zero first, they take him and not a slate lies. Find the pen. Don't make me ask you twice."
She is quiet for a moment, and her fingers stop on the rod. "Then Varka can open her shelves. The Leaking Vat is yours now, and the Basin will trade without a question. Thank you. I mean that."

"Ruthven's sweep, a magnesium flash-charge, and a crutch of ash-wood. The leg is a bad joke and the ear is worse. I can hear a bone-cipher click at forty paces and nothing on my right. Don't stand there."

entries.name: Widow Varka at the Leaking Vat
entries.speaker: widow_varka

nodes.text: Behind a veil of waxed black crepe, Widow Varka lays a pair of brass salt-scales on the sluice rail. "Everything has a price, dear. Mine are fair, and so is my memory."

choices.text: Why open the Basin to us?

nodes.text: "Rock Salt. Warded Tallow, by the day. Poultices. Whatever the Clerisy has sworn is not for sale, and is. I do not ask what you intend to burn."
"The boy ran my messages before Talia hid him. A woman remembers who feeds a child. The Basin trades with whoever brought him home. That is all the sentiment I can afford."
Ivo sits cross-legged on the Basin steps, still wearing the Toll-Pen number on his shirt. He is twelve, and he is not smiling. "Talia says you took the lock off the pen."

choices.text: What did you see in the pen?

nodes.text: "Ash-Crawl runners aren't safe. We're quick." He almost smiles. "I'll run for you if you want. Whistle twice."
"They count you in tallies of four. When the count's short, they pick the smallest. I counted the sentries instead. There's a gap at the third bell, when they change the chalk."

nodes.speaker: ivo
nodes.text: They let you go.
A hunchbacked figure mutters over a bench of calcified shards, forging a seal onto a strip of bone. "Mind the dust. It bites."
"Quarrels that open mail. Cestuses with barbs for the knuckles. Bone is dull, bone is honest, bone doesn't dream. Bring shards and a cause."
"Black-iron wedges from the Fourth Kiln. Heavy enough to split a mould and fine enough to cut a cestus. Tell the big fellow I owe him. Tell Berek I owe him more."

entries.name: Bailiff Corvo at the Third Ward gate
entries.speaker: bailiff_corvo

nodes.text: Bailiff Corvo leans on the gate-post with a stiff leg that has already turned to grey stone to the knee. "Third Ward gate. You want through, you leave something at the post. Salt or Scrap. I don't care who for."

choices.text: No more tolls. Force the Third Ward gate.
What do you keep behind the gate?

nodes.text: He takes the salt, tucks it into a ledger he doesn't write in, and nods. "Patrols cut short on the Third Ward side tonight. My sister Ida is sixteen and the Tithing is looking for sixteens. If it ever goes badly, don't make it worse."

He pockets the Scrap, tucks it into a ledger he doesn't write in, and nods. "Patrols cut short on the Third Ward side tonight. My sister Ida is sixteen and the Tithing is looking for sixteens. If it ever goes badly, don't make it worse."
"My sister. Ida. Sixteen. I keep the gate so I can keep her indoors. I kept my mind on clean water. It buys me a stone leg and a few more months."

nodes.speaker: bailiff_corvo
nodes.text: Corvo waves you off the post.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Maren kneels by the broken cages and presses grey linen to the cage seals, copying the Clerisy's cipher letter by letter. The cages are open.

choices.text: Two cell-mates walked out of the cages.
One cell-mate walked out of the cages.
Nobody walked out of the cages.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Two cell-mates, brown-faced and coughing, grin crookedly as they slip Maren a pinch of Rock Salt each. "For the cipher," says one. "For the next cage." The cage-seal rubbings are legible, and they are not the Clerisy's words.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: One cell-mate stays, rubbing their wrists. They press a grain of Rock Salt into Maren's palm and say nothing at all. She copies the seal anyway.

nodes.speaker: maren
nodes.text: Maren folds the linen away without a word. "I'll copy what's left. The names will still be on the seals."

nodes.speaker: dunstan
nodes.text: Dunstan stands in the mill-yard with his jaw wired shut and a broken slag-ladle in one fist. Nobody has asked him to speak. He holds the ladle out, handle first.

choices.text: You're one of us now. Take the next bunk.

nodes.speaker: dunstan
nodes.text: Dunstan clamps his wired jaw and nods once, a slow mortar-stone nod. Then he points at the chute where his father's bones came down, and at the mill, and at the road. He means to see all three of them smashed. Open Party (P) to swap Dunstan into the squad from the bench.

nodes.speaker: elyse
nodes.text: Elyse wipes copper-green still-sludge from her goggles and grins crookedly through the smoke. "My mother's tenement is awake, Orlov's guild is a fortnight short of tallow, and I think I need to sit down."

choices.text: Come to the Undercroft. Take the next bunk.

nodes.speaker: elyse
nodes.text: "I make alum tonic. I make tallow. I make the Spent open their eyes. If that sounds like a use, I'd like to be of it." She shoulders a bandolier of phosphorus bottles and falls in beside Vesper. Open Party (P) to swap Elyse into the squad from the bench.

nodes.speaker: sabina_kress
nodes.text: Chirurgeon Sabina has a vial of black-green marrow in one hand and a scalpel in the other. The floor is already humming. "One of you may take this. Stage One. A pin's head start on what is coming. You will not thank me. Choose."

nodes.speaker: sabina_kress
nodes.text: She turns the vial in the brazier light, waiting.

nodes.speaker: sabina_kress
nodes.text: The vial goes down a throat. Sabina does not watch.
